guide.headline: Ravens run wild while Titans deep balls die in the air
guide.hook: Lamar Jackson and a dominant Baltimore ground game face a Titans defense that can't stop the run, while Tennessee's offense has almost no answer for the deep ball.

items.title: Lamar Jackson resetting under pressure
items.what: Lamar Jackson is completing at a rate 7.2 points above expected with 9.8 yards per attempt and four touchdowns against one interception this season. Watch his feet when the first read is covered, because he's in the top 6 percent of NFL quarterbacks right now and his legs have already added 124 rush yards. He's on the field for 100 percent of Baltimore's offensive snaps, so every possession runs through him.
items.when: Every dropback, especially when the first read is covered

items.title: Ravens run game vs Titans front
items.what: The Ravens rank No. 3 of 32 in rush success rate at 51 percent, and the Titans rank No. 19 against the run at 43 percent, a 52 percentile point gap. That's a clear edge for Baltimore to stay on schedule, shorten third downs, and bleed clock. Watch the Ravens rushing attempts by halftime, north of 20 means the plan is working.
items.when: First drive and every early-down snap

items.title: Titans deep shots go nowhere
items.what: Tennessee ranks dead last in the league in pass explosiveness at 0.93, while Baltimore ranks No. 11 of 32 at limiting explosive passes at 1.26, a 68 percentile point gap. This is a prominent mismatch, the deep ball is the lowest-percentage play on the field for the Titans. Watch the longest Titans completion of the day, if it's under 25 yards at the half, the Ravens have already won this matchup.
items.when: Any Titans play-action shot downfield, check again at halftime

guide.cardLine: Lamar Jackson and a run game that's No. 3 in the league face a Titans defense that can't stop anyone on the ground or deep.
